outlook: Partisan seats; May 19 Democratic primaries in D1, D2, D5, D6, with a D5 Democratic runoff (Tucker vs Willis) on June 16. Farrior appears as the D1 Democratic nominee on Nov 3 ballot guides. Four of seven seats appear up, so the board majority is in play. Primary/runoff winners other than Farrior unverified; Cloud's incumbency (per BallotReady) unverified.
impact: The board oversees Montgomery Public Schools, home of the Star Academy at McIntyre Comprehensive Academy; it appoints the superintendent and approves vendor contracts, so turnover in four seats could reshape program renewal decisions.
result_note: Superintendent is appointed by the board (not elected). Nov 3 nominees beyond D1 not confirmed.

office: Mobile County Board of School Commissioners (Districts 3 and 4)
outlook: Two of five seats (six-year terms) up in 2026. District 3: longtime incumbent Crenshaw (D, since 2008) faces independent Meika Gordon Gardner on Nov 3. District 4 (board president Dillihay-McDade, term ends 2026): no 2026 candidate info found; her candidacy and party are unverified.
impact: MCPSS runs the STAR Academy at The Pathway 6-8 (2161 Butler St., Mobile); the board appoints the superintendent and approves the program contract. Two seats will not flip the majority, but the president's seat is up.
result_note: Superintendent is appointed (not elected). A county results page reportedly showed Crenshaw 279 (60%) vs Gardner 186 (40%) dated ~77 days before today; likely test data, treat as unverified.

office: Russell County 4.5-mill countywide school property tax renewal (revote)
outlook: Failed on May 19, 2026 (3,081 against, 2,514 for; about 13% turnout). Back on the Nov 3 ballot. Not a new tax or rate increase; renews a 30-year levy. Phenix City's separate 4-mill renewal also failed (1,146 to 1,132) and is also being revoted.
impact: Funds Russell County Schools, home of the Star site at Russell County Middle School; a second failure costs about $5.7 million a year (about $60 million over 30 years) and would squeeze discretionary spending like the Star contract.
result_note: May 19 result: FAILED. Nov 3 result pending.

office: Russell County Board of Education (At-Large, District 1, District 2)
outlook: The Nov 3 sample ballot lists Board of Education At-Large, District 1 and District 2 seats (three of seven). Candidate names and parties not retrievable; unverified. A ballot preview also mentions a 'Consolidated County School System Merger' question; its applicability to Russell County is unverified.
impact: Board oversees Russell County Middle School's Star program and must manage budget cuts if the tax revote fails again. Superintendent believed appointed, not elected (unverified).

outlook: Held with the March 3 preferential primary. Zone 2: Robertson beat incumbent Calhoun 568 to 292 (certified) and was then elected board president. Zone 5 was reopened for 2026 after community pressure. Zone 1, 3 and 5 outcomes unverified.

office: Pine Bluff School District 47.7-mill annual school tax
outlook: Listed on the Jefferson County March 3 ballot (rate set after an August 2023 election). Outcome not found; presumably routine continuation, unverified.
impact: Core operating levy for PBSD, which hosts Star at Pine Bluff Junior High and co-funds ARESC's Explore Academy.

office: ARESC member district boards: Watson Chapel (At-Large, Zone 1), White Hall (At-Large 1), Sheridan, Stuttgart
outlook: Arkansas school elections now run with the March 3 primary. Watson Chapel and White Hall candidates listed (incumbency unverified); results not found. Sheridan race info not found.
impact: ARESC (Pine Bluff) operates Explore Academy (Star curriculum, NOLA Program of the Year) and Focus Academy for member districts Pine Bluff, Sheridan, Stuttgart, Watson Chapel and White Hall; member boards fund the co-op seats.

outlook: No 2026 race or millage information found (Arkansas County). Unverified.
impact: Stuttgart SD hosts Star at Stuttgart Junior High and is an ARESC member.

impact: Board governs Central High School, the Star site; any board change affects contract renewal.

impact: Single-campus district (about 284 to 309 students) hosting Star at Strong High School; small-district finances make the contract sensitive to board shifts.

outlook: Ballotpedia lists next election March 3, 2026; seven members, three-year terms. No candidates or results found.
impact: Board governs Camden Fairview Middle School, the Star site.

office: Jefferson County School District Board of Education, District 5
outlook: Four-way nonpartisan race on Nov 3 (WLBT list; incumbency unverified; Mississippi may require a runoff if no majority). Boards are elected; all Mississippi superintendents have been board-appointed since 2019. No current state takeover/conservatorship found.
impact: Board governs Jefferson County Middle (Fayette), the Star site, and appoints the superintendent who signs the contract.

office: West Tallahatchie School District Board of Trustees
outlook: Five members, five-year terms; Ballotpedia shows Cora Hooper's term ending 2026, but no 2026 ballot listing found (unverified). Board elected; superintendent appointed. No conservatorship found; high school's third-party ranking fell to 1 star in 2025-26.
impact: Board governs West Tallahatchie Middle, the Star site; leadership has turned over repeatedly, so board stability matters for renewal.

office: Hardeman County Board of Education (District 1 Pos. 2 and 3, District 3 Pos. 2, others)
outlook: Disputed. The TN Democratic Party's primary board set aside the May 5 District 1 results (Woods and McKinnie) over absentee-ballot interference; Polk ran unopposed in D1 Pos. 2 and Stewart faced Hadley in D1 Pos. 3 on Aug 6. State Division of Elections requested a criminal investigation; Woods contests her removal.
impact: Board governs Bolivar Middle, the Star site; seat disputes and possible litigation could distract the board during contract cycles.
result_note: Aug 6 unofficial results posted by Hatchie Press but totals not retrieved; winners unverified.

office: Haywood County School Board, Districts 4 and 10 (unexpired term); Aug 6 regular seats
outlook: Three independents contest an unexpired term on Nov 3 (WREG guide). Regular school board seats were on the Aug 6 county general; results posted at haywoodvotes.com but not retrieved (unverified).
impact: Board governs Haywood Middle (Brownsville), the Star site.

office: Jackson-Madison County Board of Education (District 4 Pos. 1, District 5 Pos. 2, others)
outlook: D4 Pos. 1: board chair Walden (R) led Spotts (D) 1,589 to 1,582, a 7-vote unofficial margin. D5 Pos. 2: Marcia Moss died July 18 but won (1,809 votes); the county commission appoints an interim and voters pick a successor later. Party labels for D5 candidates unverified.
impact: Board governs North Parkway Middle, the Star site, and is evaluating Superintendent Marlon King; a razor-thin chair race and a vacancy could shift votes on contracts.
winner: Harvey Walden (D4 Pos. 1, unofficial); Marcia Moss (D5 Pos. 2, posthumous, seat vacant)
result_note: Unofficial; certification of the 7-vote margin unverified.
